about: The sheet for the Main Street Station cutaway: tools/cutaway/sheet.py. Callouts are anchored to drawn parts (history ids, in the isometric view and the flat section); a badge's style is the anchored part's confidence unless `confidence` says otherwise. Callout text is a working draft, written with Claude, for the artist to edit.
title: Main Street Station, 1952
subtitle: Cut down the middle, from Main Street up to the trains
sectionCaption: The same cut, seen flat: Main Street on the left, the trains on the right

callouts.title: Main Street
callouts.text: The station stands on the north side of East Main Street, in Shockoe Valley.

callouts.title: The loggia
callouts.text: Five arches of rough-hewn stone. Its first bay from the west opens on the main stair.

callouts.title: The main stair
callouts.text: Straight up from the Main Street doors to the waiting room, with a landing halfway, between tiled walls.

callouts.title: The waiting room
callouts.text: Most of the first floor, under a coffered ceiling, with a screen of columns and glazed arches toward the stair. Its east half is lifted away.

callouts.title: The concourse
callouts.text: An ell behind the head house, open to the shed. Five arches lead to it from the waiting room.

callouts.title: The gates
callouts.text: A wrought-iron screen between the concourse and the shed, with numbered gates to the platforms.

callouts.title: Platforms and tracks
callouts.text: Six tracks end under the shed, with a through track under each eave and five platforms, all level with the waiting room.

callouts.title: The trains
callouts.text: Seaboard Air Line trains used the west side, Chesapeake and Ohio trains the east.

callouts.title: A diesel
callouts.text: Drawn plain and generic: no source shows the engine of a train standing here.

callouts.title: The train shed
callouts.text: Riveted steel by Wilson Brothers of Philadelphia, 1900, 123 by 517 ft: trusses of 123-ft span, 18 ft apart, with a monitor on the ridge.

callouts.title: On trestles
callouts.text: Steel trestles carry the tracks, and bridges carry them over Main Street.

callouts.title: Mail and baggage
callouts.text: Baggage rooms and a public hall on the ground floor; the mail room under the concourse, docks on the west.

callouts.title: Offices
callouts.text: Railroad offices on three floors, on a corridor running east and west; two floors are in the roof, lit by dormers.

callouts.title: The clock tower
callouts.text: Six stories at the southwest corner, with a clock on each face. Its finial stands 110 ft above the ground.

key: drawn from a plan, a section or a survey map
marksNote: The same marks, small, stand before each place the trains went.
sources: Sources: HAER VA-4, the train shed (measured drawings, 1970; photographs, 1971), and HABS VA-848, the station (data pages, 1969; photographs), Library of Congress; National Register (1970) and Landmark (1976) nominations; Detroit Publishing photographs, about 1905; Library of Congress blog, 2026; SAH Archipedia; Official Guide, December 1952; OpenStreetMap; USGS 3DEP.
notes: The head house's east half is lifted away down to its ground floor, and part of the shed's roof; their outlines are dashed. No plan of the head house is known: its rooms follow the written survey, its heights are scaled from photographs. In 1952 Virginia law segregated the waiting rooms; this sheet does not show where, as no source found says where.
